skill.name: global-error-handling
skill.description: Implement robust error handling with user-friendly messages, specific exception types, fail-fast validation, centralized error boundaries, graceful degradation, and proper resource cleanup. Use this skill when writing try-catch blocks, raising exceptions, handling API errors, validating input, implementing error boundaries, managing external service failures, or ensuring resource cleanup. Apply when working with error handling code in any language, exception classes, error middleware, API error responses, retry logic, or any code that needs to handle failures gracefully while maintaining system stability and providing clear feedback to users.
skill.summary: Guide AI coding agents to implement consistent, user-friendly error handling patterns.
skill.author: EIS-ITS

security_audit.summary: The static path traversal signal is a markdown documentation link, not executable filesystem access. No prompt injection, data exfiltration intent, or malicious behavior was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.issue: Upward relative documentation link may fail outside the source repository.
remediation.suggestion: Package the referenced guidance inside the skill directory or replace the link with a same-directory reference.

finding_verdicts.reason: The traversal sequence appears only in a markdown link to project documentation. There is no executable code, user-controlled path input, or instruction to access sensitive files.

content.value_statement: Inconsistent error handling can hide failures and confuse users. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code toward clear exceptions, validation, cleanup, and recovery paths.
actual_capabilities: Guides try-catch and exception handling decisions.
Promotes specific exception types instead of generic failures.
Encourages fail-fast input validation and precondition checks.
Supports API error responses and centralized error middleware.
Covers retry strategies, graceful degradation, and cleanup logic.
limitations: Provides guidance, not a runnable error handling framework.
Does not include language-specific implementation files.
Depends on the agent applying the referenced standards correctly.
The detailed standard is linked outside the skill directory.

use_cases.title: Harden API Failure Paths
use_cases.description: Review API handlers for validation, typed errors, safe responses, retries, and cleanup.

use_cases.title: Add Frontend Error Boundaries
use_cases.description: Design user-friendly fallback behavior for React or similar frontend components.

use_cases.title: Standardize Team Error Patterns
use_cases.description: Apply one error handling approach across services, tools, and shared libraries.

prompt_templates.title: Review Basic Error Handling
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the global-error-handling skill to review this function for missing validation, unclear errors, and cleanup gaps.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a single function.

prompt_templates.title: Design API Error Responses
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the global-error-handling skill to design consistent API error responses for validation, authorization, dependency, and unexpected failures.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor Exception Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the global-error-handling skill to refactor this module so it uses specific exception types, preserves causes, and avoids swallowing errors.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Resilient Service Failure Handling
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the global-error-handling skill to create an error strategy for retries, timeouts, fallback behavior, monitoring, and resource cleanup.

output_examples.input: Review a file upload handler that catches every exception and returns a generic failure.
output_examples.output: The review identifies missing file validation, overly broad exception handling, absent cleanup for temporary files, and unclear user messages.

output_examples.input: Design error handling for a payment API that calls an external provider.
output: Validate request data before calling the provider.
Separate declined payments from provider outages.
Use bounded retries only for transient failures.
Return user-safe messages and log operational details.

best_practices: Validate inputs and preconditions before starting side effects.
Use specific error types and preserve the original cause.
Clean up resources in finally blocks or equivalent mechanisms.
anti_patterns: Catching all exceptions and continuing without action.
Showing internal stack traces or secrets to end users.
Retrying every failure without limits or classification.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps AI agents design and review robust error handling across application code.

faq.question: Does it generate a complete framework?
faq.answer: No. It provides implementation guidance that should be adapted to the target language and project.

faq.question: Can it help with frontend applications?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guidance for error boundaries, fallback behavior, and user-friendly messages.

faq.question: Can it help with backend APIs?
faq.answer: Yes. It supports validation, typed failures, API responses, middleware, retries, and cleanup.

faq.question: Does it require special tools?
faq.answer: No. It is a guidance-only skill for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What should authors improve before packaging?
faq.answer: Authors should include the linked error handling standard inside the skill package for portability.
